Record date: 2129-10-24
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 10/24/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Worsening cough and persistent fatigue despite medication adherence.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax presents for a follow-up visit two weeks after his last appointment. He reports that while his wheezing has remained stable, he has experienced a resurgence of his cough, which has become more productive over the past week. The increased sputum production is now yellowish in color, suggesting a possible infectious process. He continues to feel fatigued, which he attributes to his underlying COPD and congestive heart failure. He denies any episodes of hemoptysis but has noted a slight increase in shortness of breath, particularly with exertion.
Mr. Fairfax has been compliant with the tapering schedule for prednisone and has continued to use nebulized albuterol every hour as needed. He reports that although he has been engaging in light physical activity, he struggles to maintain his endurance and experiences increased fatigue afterward.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, - weight loss, - fever, - chills, - night sweats. Pulmonary - + productive cough with yellow sputum, + mild wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain, - orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - no joint pain. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 128/74 mmHg - Heart Rate: 82 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 22 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 88% on room air.
General: The patient appears fatigued but is alert and in no acute distress.
HEENT: No nasal flaring; oropharynx clear, no signs of dehydration.
Lungs: Mild wheezing noted on auscultation; increased bronchial breath sounds; moderate expiratory wheezing with prolonged expiration; rhonchi heard bilaterally.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops; peripheral pulses intact and symmetric.
Extremities: No edema; no tenderness on palpation.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) with exacerbation; increased sputum production and cough may indicate a possible infection or bronchitis. 2. Congestive heart failure stable; no signs of fluid overload. 3. Persistent fatigue likely multifactorial, exacerbated by respiratory symptoms and underlying cardiac condition.
PLAN
1. Initiate a 7-day course of oral antibiotics (Azithromycin 500 mg daily) to address the possibility of bacterial bronchitis, given the change in sputum color. 2. Continue nebulized albuterol every hour as needed; consider re-evaluating the addition of a long-acting beta-agonist (LABA) and a long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA) at the next visit. 3. Continue oral furosemide 40 mg daily; monitor renal function and electrolytes closely in light of recent changes in symptoms. 4. Schedule follow-up in one week for re-evaluation of respiratory status, sputum characteristics, and fatigue levels. 5. Encourage patient to maintain a symptom diary, particularly noting any changes in sputum color, volume, and frequency of cough, as well as levels of fatigue post-activity.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax was discharged home with a prescription for oral Azithromycin and continued instructions for nebulized albuterol. A follow-up appointment has been scheduled for one week from today to assess his response to treatment and adjust the management plan as necessary.
